title: Permutations II
summary: Return every distinct ordering of all input values.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–8 integers in [−10,10]. Every distinct permutation appears exactly once.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare complete sets of ordered tuples. Preserve member order within each permutation and reject duplicate rows or incorrect multiplicities.

statement: Return every distinct ordering of all input values. Each ordering must use the original multiplicities. The ordering within a result matters, while the outer result list may appear in any order.

examples.explanation: Only the position of 2 distinguishes the three orderings.
The identical copies produce one ordering.
Changing the positions of distinct values gives another permutation.

constraints: 1–8 integers in [−10,10]. Every distinct permutation appears exactly once.
hints: Conceptual: Swapping equal copies does not create another ordering.
Directional: Keep remaining counts by value.
Implementation: At each position, try each distinct available value once. Consume a copy, recurse, then restore it.
complexityAnalysis: O(nU + nP) time for the fixed 21-value domain, expressed as O(nP) for P permutations, with O(n+U) auxiliary space and O(nP) output.
